html:
SMTO-GML-0044 — The Gmail account you chose isn't set up correctly

GUID: bf40598d-6a5a-4b7f-b9a0-fb68f6f0cd9f
Slug: gmail-account-invalid
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • The saved entry SMTO used as your Gmail account is either not a Gmail account or is missing required details. SMTO stopped before contacting Gmail, so nothing changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the @ name you used. Select More options › Parameter Store and confirm that name is your Gmail account, not another saved item. Using the name of a server or password entry makes SMTO treat it as a Gmail account.
  2. If the name is right, open that entry and check the email address and other details are filled in. Don't change the email or the saved sign-in fields. A missing or mistyped detail makes the account fail SMTO's checks, while the sign-in fields must stay as they are.
  3. If the account was connected through Google sign-in and still fails, ask SMTO to reconnect it under the same name, for example 'Connect Gmail using @gmail_auth_app and save the account as work_gmail'. Reconnecting saves fresh, correct sign-in details for that account.

What success looks like

  • SMTO uses the account without this error and completes your Gmail request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the saved account, and don't paste passwords or tokens into the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected account reference resolved to a Parameter Store record that is not a Gmail or Google account type, or whose fields fail the account template's validation (gmail_account_invalid).

What this means

  • GmailParameterProfiles.resolve finds a non-gmail_account record under the selected key or its typed account fields fail validation. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • GmailParameterProfiles.resolve finds a non-gmail_account record under the selected key or its typed account fields fail validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact key, profile_type and rejected template field while preserving private token values.

How to fix it

  • Open the referenced key in Parameter Store: profile_type must be gmail_account, google_account or gmail_app_password_account and pass template validation (for gmail_account: service 'gmail', non-empty email and token_type, a canonical oauth_app_ref, and, when set, an ISO-8601 expires_at with a timezone). Point the request at the correct key, or repair the record without changing email, oauth_app_ref or stored tokens; if the tokens are damaged, reconnect the same key with gmail.connect.
  • Edit the exact Gmail account parameter using its template; preserve account identity and stored OAuth token fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended current account record passes its typed profile contract.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
